To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
6-second glance sequences are predictive of: radio tuning, talking on the phone, failure to signal a turn, and the presence of an object in the driver's field-of-view.

(1) glance can be used to predict radio-tuners, fatigue state, talking, failure to signal left, failure to signal right, and environment state; (2) glance-based predictors are robust to the number of training examples; (3) the predictive power of glance-based predictors is not significantly different than that of the state-of-the-art; (4) the predictive power increases with glance duration; and (5) glance-based predictors generalize to unseen drivers and environments.

(1) 6-second sequences of macro-glances can predict radio tuning and talking; (2) 6-second sequence macro-glances can infer fatigue, distraction, failure to signal; and (3) 6-second macro-glance sequences can infer environment variables such as road type, road condition, and weather condition.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the question: can we predict the state of the world from driver glances? We answer that question with a resounding yes, and that such prediction is possible even with only six seconds of glance data.

the state of the art in driver gaze estimation can be used for driver monitoring and safety applications.
the state of the world and the state of driver can be predicted with 70% accuracy from a 6-seconds sequence of driver glances.
glance is a rich, reliable, and informative signal, and it is a valuable component of a multi-sensory system for driver state estimation.

driver glance data can be used to predict a variety of driver state variables and environment variables.
